heuristics: Smoothness probabilities, relation counts and the factor-base size use Dickman's rho with the GS21 alpha correction, as estimated by the GS21 simulator. This is the standard heuristic basis of NFS analyses and is not re-proved here; the published Table 10 parameters are used as published rather than re-optimised.

The individual-logarithm descent is priced explicitly, not absorbed: L[1/3,1.44] by Barbulescu-Pierrot, evaluated at N=p^12 as exp(1.44*59.033894749678)=2^122.641786367599 model operations, and added to the core. An earlier revision of this ledger priced it at 2^85 and claimed 28 bits of headroom; that was wrong and is corrected here, at a cost of 0.1218 bits.
The ECM cofactorization of the smoothness tests is charged at 2^87.6 model operations and added; it is 2^-38.7 of the core.

The model-to-instruction conversion charges 1024 scalar instructions per GS21 model operation. The largest conversion that follows from published data is 11.31 cycles per model operation (BD19 Table 6, worst measured/model ratio 2^3.5) times 8 scalar instructions per cycle (widest current AArch64 retirement) = 90.5; the charge is 11.3x that. A larger charge can only weaken the claim, so this factor cannot make the bound too small.

The retry multiplicity is charged as 2 (a single capped attempt assumed to succeed with probability only 1/2, while the published simulation overshoots the factor base by 2^0.54). E[T] <= 2*B is the left side of a Markov inequality; no expectation is reported as an upper bound on the work of a single run.

The run is hard-truncated at 2*E[T]=4*B instructions and returns FAILURE at the cap, so the submitted work bound is the enforced cap. Markov gives success probability at least 1/2 over uniform P, uniform z and fresh coins.
The matrix weight (200), filtering factor (20), block-Wiedemann word cost (4 words), sieving volume (2*686+1)^12/2 and smoothness bound 2^65.316 are GS21's published model constants for BLS-381.
limitations: This is an analytic reproduction of a published cost model at production parameters, not an executed 2^123 computation; the rules allow an analytic argument for exponentially large attacks.

The 2023 BD19-based survey figure 2^122.54 for BLS12-381 is not used because it is not reproducible from its own stated parameters (its sieving space alone is 2^122.85 and its factor-base count does not follow from its stated A=2); the self-consistent GS21 total is the conservative choice.

The 1024 instructions-per-model-operation charge is a deliberate over-charge, not a measurement. It is the largest single concession in the submission: a bare 90.5-instruction reading of the published calibration would give a score 4.5 bits lower.

Storage is reported per instance and is not the scored objective on this track; the relation file at 2^72.389800 bytes is far beyond any single machine and the schedule is a merging-stream design, not an executed one.
The descent constant 1.44 is asymptotic; it is used at full weight rather than discounted.

challenge_input.fixed_argument: P in G1, nonidentity, uniform and fixed per instance (not necessarily the generator P0)
challenge_input.target: z in GT, uniform, may be the identity

verification.method: one pairing check e(P,Q)=z (all twelve coefficients) and one subgroup check [r]Q=O
